system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| ID / issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation (one-line reason) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | Aggregate cap of **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)** for general Warranty Claims. | A materially higher cap, preferably the full price or a negotiated amount aligned with potential exposure; separate, higher caps for tax and IP if needed. | **Reject and negotiate upward**—AUD 4.8m may not cover material warranty losses in a AUD 24m acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis per claim; AUD 250,000 tipping/excess-only basket. | A lower de minimis and a tipping basket (recover all qualifying claims once the basket is crossed), or a deductible basket only if the price reflects it. | **Seek a lower de minimis and tipping basket**—the proposed thresholds exclude smaller claims and make the Buyer absorb the first AUD 250,000. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion; Seller also proposes applying any limitation to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period for general warranties, with tax claims running through the relevant statutory period plus a buffer; no deadline should cut across separately negotiated claims or indemnities. | **Reject the blanket extension to all Claims and negotiate longer, claim-specific periods**—18 months may be too short, and distinct claims need distinct survival rules. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties. | Separate, substantially higher or uncapped liability and longer survival for capacity, authority and title warranties. | **Reject**—title and capacity are core to acquiring 100% of the shares and should not share the general-warranty cap or short sunset. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | No express fraud carve-out is stated; Seller says limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims. | Expressly exclude fraud (including fraudulent misrepresentation and deliberate concealment) from caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the extent legally permissible. | **Require an express carve-out**—otherwise the Seller may argue contractual limits restrict remedies for its own fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the indexed data room, Accounts, registers and public records, including DD-002 to DD-012. | Specific, fair disclosure against each warranty, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-records disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure and require warranty-specific disclosure**—a broad data-room dump can qualify warranties without clear notice of the relevant risk. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | No “constructive knowledge” bar; at most, limit it to actual knowledge of named individuals after reasonable inquiry, and preserve claims for fraud and specific indemnities. | **Reject the proposed qualifier**—mere discoverability improperly shifts diligence risk to Buyer and rewards inadequate disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure says no final consent or evidence conditions are satisfied. | A condition precedent requiring final written consent and satisfaction or waiver of all contractual conditions before Completion, with termination rights if not obtained. | **Make it a completion condition**—Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and consent alone may not satisfy clause 11.3. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure confirms no repayment or final security discharge is included. | Repayment at or before Completion from Seller proceeds, with lender payout evidence and executed releases/discharges delivered at Completion; no residual target debt or security. | **Require simultaneous payoff and discharge**—a post-Completion promise leaves Buyer exposed to debt and continuing security over the Company’s assets. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are not separately itemised in the draft funds flow; treatment of payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs is unstated. | Identify all bonus entitlements and on-costs, determine whether they are debt-like or otherwise price-adjusting, and have Seller fund or provide for them in the completion accounts/funds flow. | **Reconcile and allocate the full cost before signing off funds flow**—unprovided bonuses and on-costs could reduce the value delivered to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; DD-004/010 show AUD 180,000 open, but no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | A specific indemnity covering payment, transfer/ownership and use of all relevant Project Materials, with payment/discharge and assignment evidence as a Completion deliverable. | **Expand the protection and require evidence**—the SOW3 transfer is conditional on clearing every fee, and the record does not verify payment or assignment. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Seller characterises DD-006 as preliminary and not expected to be material; disclosure says access, scope and notification requirements are unknown. | Full incident facts and investigation results; appropriate pre-Completion remediation and notification compliance; a specific indemnity for incident-related liabilities, costs and claims. | **Do not accept a materiality assumption; seek a specific indemnity and closing protections**—the exposed dataset may contain about 1,240 people’s records and the risk remains unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals total AUD 330,000, described as ordinary-course costs. Disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Review terms, timing and termination rights; identify accrued or committed liabilities and treat unusual or post-Completion obligations appropriately in price/working capital and warranties. | **Do not accept the “ordinary-course” label without evidence**—the disclosure does not establish the renewals’ economic or contractual effect. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Seller says limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to Claims of any nature; general limitation language may also apply absent express exceptions. | Separate regimes for warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, debt/price adjustments and fraud, with express priority and carve-outs from general limitations. | **Require express category-by-category drafting**—a blanket regime risks unintentionally capping or barring claims intended to be separately protected. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register showing it holds 100% of issued shares; it does not say Buyer has independently verified title. | Verify the register against constitutional and ASIC records and require title warranties, transfer instruments and any required corporate approvals at Completion. | **Verify independently and retain robust title protections**—the register is evidence to check, not a substitute for clean transfer and title warranties. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime; no specific tax/IP terms are supplied here. | Obtain and negotiate express tax and IP warranty scope, tailored caps and survival, and specific indemnities for identified risks; confirm interaction with general limitations. | **Treat these as unresolved until documented**—a general cap/time-limit position does not establish adequate tax or IP protection. |
=== END ADVICE ===
